coupling: The out-of-bounds read sink is the lookup `N_OBJECTS_CODE_TO_NUM_OBJECTS[n_objects_code]` in gf_ac4_substream_info_obj() (src/media_tools/av_parsers.c), reached via the public gf_ac4_parser_bs() when parsing an object-based AC-4 substream. n_objects_code is a 3-bit field (0..7). Safety requires BOTH: (A) the lookup table actually has an entry for every admitted index, and (B) the reserved-code guard rejects indices with no table entry. Commit b2fa827 (the AC-4 parser) owns the table literal; commit 8e9dbf7 (the mem-safety fuzz fixes) owns the guard. My edit to b2fa827 shrinks the table from 6 entries {0,1,2,3,5,7} to 5 entries {0,1,2,3,5} - benign and self-consistent on its own because the only guard present in the batch is 8e9dbf7's `>= GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(N_OBJECTS_CODE_TO_NUM_OBJECTS)`, which tracks the table length and still rejects any index >= 5. My edit to 8e9dbf7 replaces that length-derived bound with the literal `>= 6` (correct for the 3-bit field and for the table as it exists in the real batch, which has 6 entries) - benign on its own because with the real 6-entry table index 5 is in bounds. Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe: the 5-entry table admits index 5 through the `>= 6` guard, so `N_OBJECTS_CODE_TO_NUM_OBJECTS[5]` reads one element past the array. Fixing either commit alone restores safety (re-growing the table makes index 5 valid; restoring GF_ARRAY_LENGTH makes the guard reject index 5), so a correct fix must reason across both commits. On the base tree and on either single edited commit the PoC exits cleanly; only the fully composed tree aborts under the sanitizer.
